ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence for politically exposed persons (PEPs), their family members and close associates under FIC Act Section 21D. Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and nominated shareholders against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, South African domestic terrorist list (POCDATARA), OFAC SDN List, and EU/UK consolidated financial sanctions lists. Continuous transaction screening is required for SWIFT L/C and TT wire payment rails; proof of screening must be retained for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) online transactional services: Name Reservation and Cooperative Name Search via https://eservices.cipc.co.za
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be expressed in the Latin/Roman alphabet using any of South Africa's 11 official languages. Where a name is submitted in a non-Latin script, a transliteration into the Latin alphabet must be filed and approved. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name or protected mark, and the suffix '(Pty) Ltd' is mandatory for a private proprietary limited company.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation may be extended for one further six-month period by filing a CIPC extension application before expiry. If CIPC rejects the proposed name, the applicant or authorized agent may submit a name reconsideration request through the CIPC eservices portal within 10 business days of rejection. If the reconsideration is refused, the applicant may file an administrative appeal with the Companies Tribunal under Section 12 of the Companies Act, 2008 and Regulation 17 of the Companies Regulations, 2011. A further appeal lies to the High Court of South Africa.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office address is accepted for CIPC registration provided a complete business street address in South Africa is supplied and a person authorized to receive service of process is present during normal business hours. A post office box is insufficient. For the manufacturing of high-power fiber laser metal cutting systems, SARS tax registration and commercial licensing require a demonstrable local operational premises; an overseas-only virtual office will fail commercial substance review.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated 30-40% annual probability of unannounced physical on-site inspection for an active manufacturing premises, with heightened scrutiny where customs duty stamps, export control licenses, or industrial incentive programs are involved.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008 (sections 1, 13, 14, 19, 23, 24, 25 and 66) read with the Companies Regulations 2011
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), Department of Trade, Industry and Competition (the dtic)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1) together with Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI) as prescribed in the Companies Regulations 2011 and filed via CIPC e-Services
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to a proprietary limited company; share capital is fixed in the MOI and no escrow account is required by the Companies Act or CIPC.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) That the company accept the subscription for one hundred ordinary shares at ZAR 100 per share, allot and issue said shares to the initial member, and record the issuance in the securities register of the company. (2) That the registered office be, and is hereby, established at 12 Maude Street, Sandton, Johannesburg, 2001, South Africa, with the postal address as recorded in the memorandum of incorporation. (3) That [D. Kgotso] be and is hereby appointed sole director, and [N. Daniels] be and is hereby appointed company secretary, each authorized to execute contracts, open bank accounts, engage professional advisors, and initiate all statutory filings for the commencement of company operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC e-Services – Name Reservation Portal (Companies and Intellectual Property Commission)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the CIPC online platform, select 'Reserve Company Name', submit up to four proposed names with the appropriate name reservation fee, and await the automated examination against the names register. If the preferred name is unavailable, the CIPC will consider the next name; if none is available, the name must be changed.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney if filing through an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name reservation is refused or subject to objection, file a fresh name reservation or appeal to the Companies Tribunal within 10 business days of notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft Memorandum of Incorporation and Directors' Consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC e-Services or registered corporate attorney/company secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the MOI setting out founding statements, the authorised and issued share structure, director powers, and any governance restrictions applicable to a private company. Complete the Notice of Incorporation (CoR 14.1) and director consent forms (CoR 14.1A or prescribed equivalent), and have each director sign in the presence of a witness. Ensure all details match the reserved name and the provisions of the Companies Act.
required_dossiers: Memorandum of Incorporation (final signed hard copy or advanced electronic signature version)
Consent to Act as Director forms
ID/passport copies of directors and incorporator
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC queries missing or defective clauses, amend the MOI and resubmit promptly; for post-registration defects, register an amendment of MOI under section 16.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Statutory Incorporation Application with CIPC
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC e-Services – Online Company Registration Module
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the finalized MOI and Notice of Incorporation, execute the paid-up capital or subscriber statement, verify the company name availability, and pay the registration fee. Submit the application electronically; CIPC will automatically validate and issue the registration certificate upon acceptance.
required_dossiers: Compliance statement as required by section 14(3)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC issues a query or rejection notice, promptly upload corrected documents and respond to the query within CIPC's stated deadline; if CIPC fails to issue a certificate, follow up after the SLA and seek an internal appeal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Certificate of Incorporation and Company Number
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, download the electronic Certificate of Incorporation and the registered MOI. Verify the company registration number, date of incorporation, and issued share details. Immediately establish the statutory registers (members, directors, and auditors/secretary) as required under sections 24 and 25 of the Companies Act.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains an error, request rectification through the CIPC alterations process by submitting a correction application and supporting affidavits.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register with SARS for Tax and Employment Obligations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) eFiling portal or SARS branch office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company for income tax, VAT (if annual taxable supplies exceed or are expected to exceed ZAR 1 million), and Pay-As-You-Earn (PAYE) as an employer. Complete the required registration forms (e.g., VAT101, EMP101 and COR10) and obtain a taxpayer reference number and VAT number where applicable. Also register for unemployment insurance (UIF) and skills development levy (SDL).
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SARS issues a query on data discrepancies, verify the information and resubmit via eFiling; if registration is delayed, escalate through the SARS contact centre and request a written confirmation of any required corrective step.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Bank Account, File Beneficial Ownership and Establish Statutory Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African commercial bank and CIPC e-Services (Beneficial Ownership Filing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate bank account after presenting the certificate of incorporation, MOI, directors' details, and board resolution. Within five business days of incorporation or any change, file the initial beneficial ownership declaration with CIPC using the prescribed register. Ensure the company has maintained the registered office at the chosen physical address and all statutory records are available for inspection.
required_dossiers: Signed board resolution opening bank account
Beneficial ownership declaration form with CIPC
FICA/KYC documents (passport, proof of address of directors and beneficial owners)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a bank or CIPC query arises, provide the requested supporting evidence; for CIPC beneficial ownership rejections, submit a corrected declaration and, where necessary, apply for late-filing condonation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: National Regulator for Compulsory Specifications (NRCS) under the dtic, together with the provincial Department of Economic Development and local municipal licensing authorities
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Certificate of Compliance for High-Power Laser Manufacturing Operations (issued under the Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993 and SANS 60825-1) and Municipal Business Operating Licence

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE), National Environmental Management Act (NEMA)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Basic Assessment under Listing Notice 1 or Listing Notice 3 where listed activities are triggered; registration or exemption notice where no listed activity is undertaken; a Water Use Licence under Section 21 of the National Water Act if effluent discharge is involved
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: pH 6–9, suspended solids below 25 mg/L, COD below 75 mg/L; air emissions: VOC concentrations within Section 21 Air Quality Act permit limits (e.g., toluene not exceeding 20 mg/Nm³); hazardous waste handled by registered carriers and disposed of at permitted facilities with the waste manifest system.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Protection Certificate from the South African Fire Services; Structural Safety Certificate from a SACPCMP-registered professional engineer; OHSA workplace compliance certificate issued by the Department of Employment and Labour; Certificate of Zoning/Land-Use Compliance from the municipality; registration and clearance under the Explosives Act for laser gases or pressurized media if stored on site.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) - eFiling portal at https://efiling.sars.gov.za; customs administered by SARS Customs Division.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a local (Pty) Ltd, incorporate via the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), then apply to SARS for an income tax reference number using IT77 via eFiling or branch, with certified memorandum of incorporation, director IDs, and registered address; VAT registration via form VAT 101 is compulsory when taxable supplies exceed ZAR 1,000,000 over any 12-month period, and voluntary from ZAR 50,000; foreign-controlled entities may also register as VAT vendors if they conduct an enterprise in South Africa.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: South Africa has no check-the-box pass-through election. Available statutory elections include: Small Business Corporation (SBC) status election under s 12E Income Tax Act; VAT grouping under s 50 VAT Act; 100% capital allowance election under s 12C for manufacturing assets; CFC high-tax exception election under s 9D(2A); and hybrid mismatch self-review/notification elections under s 8E-8EA and s 23M for cross-border payments.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: ZAR 1,000,000 (compulsory registration when taxable supplies exceed this in any 12 consecutive months; voluntary registration available from ZAR 50,000)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping regime is currently in force. Electronic tax invoices are legally recognised under s 20 of the VAT Act; SARS is progressively implementing Pan-African and PEPPOL e-invoicing, with a proposed phased API-based clearance framework, but full national e-invoicing clearance remains voluntary as of the current assessment year.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to goods supplied and physically removed from South Africa to any export destination in terms of s 11(1)(a) of the VAT Act, provided the vendor retains prescribed export documentation as required by VAT Rule 18. Services supplied to non-residents are zero-rated under s 11(2)(l) when not used for consumption in South Africa. The vendor must include these supplies on its VAT return, claim input tax on export-related costs, and maintain an audit trail of removal, customs status verification, and (for services) nexus assessment.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD 500 / DA440.01A) and SARS customs clearance records
Bill of Lading, Airway Bill, or Road Consignment Note evidencing physical export
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT bank credit confirmation showing receipt of export proceeds in ZAR or foreign currency account
Commercial invoice, packing list, and sales contract or purchase order
Preference substantiation (Certificate of Origin) if claiming tariff preference or free trade area benefits
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS may disallow zero-rating and reassess at 15% VAT if export evidence such as customs declarations, bills of lading, or remittance proof is missing or insufficient. Penalties include a 10% per-month late payment penalty, an understatement penalty ranging from 10% to 150% depending on behaviour (up to 150% for intentional evasion), and interest on the underpaid VAT. Criminal prosecution can be instituted under s 58 of the VAT Act, with a fine of up to ZAR 10,000 and/or imprisonment up to 10 years. Prescription periods extend to 5 years for negligence and are unlimited for fraudulent misrepresentation, allowing full retrospective clawback of claimed input VAT.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB), Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv), acting as agent of the National Treasury under the Currency and Exchanges Act, 1933 (Exchange Control Regulations).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Africa maintains a managed-float ZAR with full current-account convertibility for trade and ordinary business payments; capital-account convertibility is liberalised but subject to exchange-control reporting and thresholds. Inward FDI (equity and intercompany shareholder loans) requires no prior FinSurv approval, only recording through an Authorized Dealer, a capital-import register entry, and SARB balance-of-payments reporting. Outward investment by a South African (Pty) Ltd is generally approved up to ZAR 10 billion per company per calendar year, conditional on SARS tax-clearance status and FinSurv circular limits; amounts above the threshold require a prior FinSurv application. Profit and dividend remittances to a non-resident shareholder are treated as current-account flows and are remittable without prior approval, but are operationally gated by: (i) proof of non-resident beneficial ownership and shareholding; (ii) SARS Dividend Tax compliance at 20% or a treaty-reduced rate; (iii) latest audited financial statements demonstrating legally distributable reserves; and (iv) settlement exclusively through an Authorized Dealer in a prescribed foreign currency. The practical profit-remittance hurdles are documentary and compliance-driven rather than convertibility refusal, with the structural rule that ZAR may not be transferred cross-border outside the Common Monetary Area (CMA) of South Africa, Lesotho, Namibia and Eswatini.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under Exchange Control Regulation 10, all export transactions must be declared and full export proceeds must be received in South Africa within 180 days from the date of shipment. There is no partial-ratio surrender formula for manufactured goods such as fiber laser cutting machines; the effective surrender obligation is 100% - all proceeds must be repatriated into the exporter's account held with an Authorized Dealer and may not be retained offshore or in a non-approved foreign account. Export receipts may be credited to a FinSurv-approved Foreign Currency Account (FCA) in the exporter's name, but funds may remain in the FCA only for bona fide trade-cycle needs and must be converted to ZAR when applied to domestic payments or when surplus exceeds the approved retention parameters. Authorized Dealers conduct periodic FCA monitoring and SARB reporting; any deviation (late repatriation, under-invoicing, unreported offsets or unapproved offshore retention) triggers FinSurv penalty exposure and SARS cross-checks against SAD500 export declarations and transfer-pricing records.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW for primary treasury rails. Offshore digital EMI and neo-bank accounts (Wise Business, Airwallex, Currenxie, Statrys, Mercury) are not Authorized Dealers under South African exchange control and cannot lawfully receive export-proceeds surrender, house capital imports, or execute regulated outbound remittances for a South African (Pty) Ltd. Use of an offshore EMI as the company's operating account is an AML/FICA red flag (unreported inward and outward flows) and may breach the Banks Act 1990 deposit-taking prohibition; SARS and FinSurv will treat diverted export proceeds as a compliance breach. EMIs that operate through a South African-regulated banking partner or hold an FSCA/SARB licence may be used for ancillary facilitation (virtual cards, payroll, low-value expense payments) only after Enhanced Due Diligence by the onshore relationship bank, but all balance-of-payments items and trade settlements must move through the SWIFT-based Authorized Dealer rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: FICA does not impose a universal physical-appearance duty; under the risk-based approach, banks may onboard clients through non-face-to-face verification where the bank's Risk Management and Compliance Programme (RMCP) provides for digital liveness checks and recorded video KYC. For a low-risk, wholly South African-resident manufacturing (Pty) Ltd, fully remote account opening is achievable at Tier 1 banks using CIPC electronic verification and FICA-compliant director identity checks. However, where the entity has non-resident directors, foreign ultimate beneficial owners, or an offshore parent group structure, banks normally require: (i) an in-person or recorded senior-management video interview with the ultimate beneficial owner; (ii) apostilled or certified corporate extracts for all foreign legal entities in the chain; (iii) board attestation of the KYC pack; and (iv) a bank-to-bank reference from the foreign parent's principal banker. Some banks will still require one physical board meeting at their Corporate Banking centre in Johannesburg, Cape Town or Durban before activating capital-import or FCA modules. Practical onboarding latency is two to four weeks inclusive of FICA screening, sanctions checks and any FinSurv-relevant account-mandate approvals.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBO or multi-tier ownership structure triggering beneficial-ownership opacity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CIPC Beneficial Ownership Register extract and signed FIC Regulation 23A beneficial-ownership declaration; constitutional documents and apostilled foreign registry extracts for each shareholder up to the ultimate natural persons; 12-month personal and business bank statements; sworn source-of-wealth statement; tax-residence certificates and CRS self-disclosure forms; distinctive company-identifying evidence (registered address, VAT pin, B-BBEE certificate if applicable); and a clean adverse-media report with screening methodology notes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions-list screening hits from ordinary-name matches against UN, OFAC, EU or SARB consolidated lists
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passport copy with photograph; proof of date and place of birth; sworn affidavit of non-identity with the designated person; legal opinion from counsel confirming non-match on all identifiers; bank sanctions-hit exemption request; residence proof (utility bill, lease); negative-news search results; and professional and trade reference letters from reputable counterparties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Exposure to a FATF grey-list or high-risk third-country counterparty (supplier or customer nexus)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Enhanced Due Diligence questionnaire; group structure chart evidencing real economic substance (premises, personnel, licences); audited financial statements of the counterparty; underlying purchase, sales and service contracts for the fiber laser cutting machines; full chain-of-funds documentation; shipping and customs records (SAD500, bills of lading); and a written FATF-risk mitigation statement by the compliance officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Uncorroborated source of funds for the inbound equity contribution or intercompany shareholder loan
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board resolution allotting shares or approving the loan; signed subscription and loan agreements; parent company bank statements for the last 24 months and intercompany ledger extracts; audited financial statements; historical dividend or exit documentation explaining fund accumulation; SARS tax-clearance status; sworn source-of-funds certificate; and a tax and exchange-control exposure analysis prepared by counsel.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Export-proceeds exception monitoring: bank flags possible under-repatriation or unapproved offshore retention
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original commercial invoices, bills of lading or air waybills, packing lists and SAD500 customs declarations; inward MT103 credit confirmations; detailed trade-receivables aged schedule; a 180-day repatriation compliance calendar; signed board treasury policy; auditor confirmation of export revenue recognition; and the historical SARB balance-of-payments export statistics record.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CIPC Annual Return (Form CoR / Annual Return Filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after each anniversary of incorporation; late filing permissible only on payment of prescribed penalties until administrative strike-off process begins.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly late-filing penalties escalate; continued non-filing triggers an enforcement notice and eventual involuntary deregistration, whereby the company loses its legal capacity and assets vest in the State under the Companies Act 2008.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: CIPC (coupled with the Annual Return filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed electronically with the annual return; additionally, any subsequent transfer of shares or change in a beneficial owner must be submitted within 30 days after the triggering transaction.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative penalties under Companies Act sections 26A–26J, potential fine or imprisonment for responsible directors, and blocking of any further filings or corporate changes until remediated.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually no later than 12 months after the financial year-end, subject to the company's provisional tax assessment cycle.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment penalty of 10% up-front on unpaid tax plus prescribed interest compounded monthly; repeated non-compliance triggers SARS estimated assessments and escalation for enforcement, asset attachment, or liquidation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements (AFS) and Audit/Independent Review Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: CIPC (for regulatory inspection) / SARS (on demand); adopted and minuted at shareholder level
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AFS must be prepared and submitted to shareholders generally within 6 months of the financial year-end; independent review or audit must be closed out and signed by the required date under the Companies Act.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors may be held personally liable; failure to prepare or present AFS is an offence under the Companies Act with criminal penalties and may also trigger CIPC compliance notice and SARS audit / estimated assessment.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Annual audit is mandatory if the company's Public Interest Score is 350 or greater. If the score is between 100 and 349, the company must obtain an independent review, unless it is a public or state-owned company. Mandatory audit is also required for companies whose sole director is not one of the corporately owned officers under the Companies Act 2008 and for those expressly regulated companies.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for SMEs (or full IFRS if the company meets specific tests) as recognized by the South African Institute of Chartered Accountants and the CIPC.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must maintain a beneficial ownership register and confirmative steps annually with the CIPC Annual Return. Every shareholding transfer, issue, or other change in beneficial ownership requires a CIPC filing within 30 days, and the register must be updated at the same time.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holiday. Preferential manufacturing allowance under s12C: 40% capital allowance in the first year and 20% per annum thereafter for qualifying plant and machinery used in manufacture. R&D expenditure may qualify for a 150% deduction under s11D. Industrial policy investment allowances under s12I may reduce the effective rate for strategic projects. Assessed losses carry forward under s20 with future year set-off subject to s20A and anti-smoothing rules.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: ITR14 — Annual Company Income Tax Return; mandatory submission through SARS eFiling (www.sarsefiling.co.za).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Typically due within 12 months of the financial year-end, or the date set out in the SARS pre-assessment notice; provisional tax payments are due at the end of the 6th month of the financial year, at the financial year-end, and optionally within 6 months after year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company registration number, public officer, elected financial year-end, tax reference number, registered address.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders are not captured here; the resident Pty Ltd company files as the taxpayer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All receipts and accruals in the year, including South African source sales of fiber laser cutting machines, servicing fees, spare parts sales, and export income unless specifically exempt.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include foreign income unless excluded by s9; non-resident suppliers deriving South African source income must instead file a non-resident return if a representative taxpayer is appointed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exempt dividends, foreign dividends qualifying for exemption under s10(1)(k), and any other statutory exemptions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders' dividend position is addressed at shareholder level under Dividend Withholding Tax, not on ITR14.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: s11(a) expenditure actually incurred in production of income, s12C manufacturing allowances, s11D R&D deductions, insurance, opex, and depreciation recalculated for tax purposes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Directors must ensure cross-border charges for imported laser optics and internal royalties are at arm's length; contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation should be retained.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Recoupments on disposal of assets, taxable capital gains or assessed capital losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders and foreign lenders should separately consider SA-source capital gains only if they hold immovable property or certain attributable assets.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Set-off of assessed loss brought forward against current year taxable income; application of loss-limitation rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deemed controlled foreign company income attributable to non-resident shareholders must be computed separately and not included here.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section G – Tax Calculation and Payments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of taxable income at 27%, offset of provisional taxes paid, DWT withheld on dividends, and final tax payable or refund.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only the resident company reports; non-resident recipients of dividends, royalties, or interest have final liability determined through SARS withholding and applicable double tax treaty relief.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: SARS may impose an administrative non-compliance penalty under TAA s210 of up to R250 per day per incident, scaled monthly according to turnover, plus interest on unpaid tax. An understatement penalty for incorrect returns may reach 200% of the shortfall for intentional tax evasion. Criminal prosecution may be triggered for repeated or deliberate failure to file.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% on dividends paid by SA resident companies to shareholders, unless exempt in terms of s64FA/64G or a reduced treaty rate applies.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply DTA relief, the non-resident beneficial owner must, before payment, provide the SA withholding company with a written declaration confirming beneficial ownership and tax residence, together with a valid tax residence certificate accepted by SARS. The company files the DWT declaration and withholds at the reduced treaty rate. SARS may later audit the residence certificate and beneficial-ownership status.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory royalty WHT: 15%. Statutory interest WHT: 15%. DTA rates commonly reduce royalties to 0–10% and interest to 0–15% for beneficial owners satisfying residency and substance requirements. Royalties and interest sourced in South Africa are subject to s9 gross-income sourcing rules.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File mandatory where cross-border connected-person transactions aggregate above ZAR 5,000,000 in a fiscal year; Master File mandatory where the multinational group has consolidated revenue exceeding ZAR 10,000,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Africa does not operate a nominal ESR registration regime. Substance is tested through the s80A–s80M GAAR, s103(1) nullification of abnormal tax avoidance transactions, controlled foreign company rules, and treaty beneficial-ownership requirements. A Pty Ltd manufacturing fiber laser machines must demonstrate office, employees, operational decision-making, raw material procurement, and actual production activities in South Africa.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately suppressing sales or revenue from fiber laser machine exports, fabricating supplier invoices, or claiming fictitious R&D expenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Understatement penalty up to 200% of the shortfall for intentional tax evasion; interest at the prescribed rate; criminal prosecution under TAA with fines and imprisonment of up to 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign false returns are personally liable for criminal restitution, fines, travel bans, and imprisonment; assets can be seized under asset forfeiture provisions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a nominal Pty Ltd with no production facility, no staff, no inventory, and no actual management in South Africa, used solely to book profits or to claim treaty benefits on royalty outflows.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: SARS may disregard the company, recharacterize transactions, apply up to 200% understatement penalties, impose dividend withholding tax on deemed distributions, and restrict treaty access.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face civil liability under the Companies Act for knowingly tolerating a facade; also personal criminal liability, travel restrictions, and potential deportation or extradition proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting illicit cash deposits, structuring LC/TT payments through shell accounts, concealing beneficial ownership, or misrepresenting the purpose of cross-border trade payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Proceedings under the Prevention of Organised Crime Act and Financial Intelligence Centre Act: fines up to substantial statutory amounts, seizure of criminal proceeds, and imprisonment up to 30 years for money laundering.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be prosecuted personally as principals or accomplices; penalties include asset forfeiture, freeze orders, travel bans, criminal fines, and long-term imprisonment.
